New York Giants and Jameis Winston Agree to 2-Year Extension

by Eric Kennedy | Sep 6, 2026 | News and Notes

Jameis Winston – © USA TODAY Sports
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:51
Instaread

NEW YORK GIANTS AND JAMEIS WINSTON AGREE TO 2-YEAR EXTENSION…
The New York Giants and QB Jameis Winston have agreed to a reported 2-year, $13 million contract extension. Winston was on the last year of his 2-year, $8 million deal with his current cap number amounting to $5 million in 2026. His $3,950,000 base salary in 2026 will now likely be reduced, providing the Giants with immediate cap relief. Winston is now under contract through the 2028 season.

The Giants signed Winston as an unrestricted free agent from the Cleveland Browns in March 2025. He ended up being a pleasant surprise, not so much because of what he did on the field, but the leadership, charisma, and positivity he brought to the team. Winston was inactive as the third-string quarterback for the first 10 games of the season. After Dart suffered a concussion in Week 10, Winston started the next two games, which the Giants lost. Winston finished the year completing 56.1 percent of his passes for 567 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions. He also rushed for one touchdown.

The 6’4”, 231-pound Winston was originally drafted in the 1st round of the 2015 NFL Draft by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He has spent time with the Buccaneers (2015-2019), New Orleans Saints (2020-2023), and Browns (2024). In his 11-year career, Winston has played in 108 regular-season games with 89 starts. He is 36-53 as a starter, throwing for 24,792 yards, 156 touchdowns, and 113 interceptions.

GIANTS SIGN MALIK HARRISON TO PRACTICE SQUAD…
The Giants have signed ILB Malik Harrison to the Practice Squad and terminated the Practice Squad contract of DT Ben Barten.

The 28-year old, 6’3”, 247-pound Harrison was originally drafted in the 3rd round of the 2020 NFL Draft by the Baltimore Ravens. He has spent time with both the Ravens (2020-2024) and Pittsburgh Steelers (2025). He missed the first half of 2025 with a knee injury and the Steelers cut him in late August 2026. In six seasons, Harrison has played in 87 regular-season games with 43 starts, accruing 215 tackles, two sacks, nine tackles for losses, and one pass defense. Harrison is a physical, assignment-sound inside linebacker who plays best versus the run and can bump up on the edge in base fronts. He lacks range and consistency in coverage. Core special teams player.

The Giants claimed Barten off of waivers from the New York Jets in August 2026. The Giants had signed Barten as an undrafted rookie free agent after the 2026 NFL Draft, but waived him in late July.

DENNIS HICKEY GIVEN NEW TITLE…
Dennis Hickey, who has served the New York Giants as assistant director of player personnel since 2022, is now a senior personnel executive for the franchise. Hickey is best known for being the general manager of the Miami Dolphins in 2014-2015.
